subsystems.name: Low-frequency antenna array
subsystems.role: collects the faint metre-wave signal; the whole technique only works below roughly 200 MHz, where the emission is bright enough and the sky is quiet.
parts: station of tens to hundreds of elements

subsystems.name: Receiver and digitiser
subsystems.role: turns each antenna's analogue signal into sampled digital data across tens of megahertz of bandwidth.

subsystems.name: Beamformer and correlator
subsystems.role: combines the elements into one or more pointed beams: one on the target star, others pointed nearby to measure the background.

subsystems.name: RFI monitoring and excision
subsystems.role: removes human-made interference, which at these frequencies is far stronger than any astrophysical signal.

subsystems.name: Spectrometer and polarimeter
subsystems.role: resolves the narrow emission band and measures its circular polarisation.

subsystems.name: Detection and vetting pipeline
subsystems.role: searches stacked spectra for drifting, polarised narrowband features and filters out false positives.

buildSteps.title: Select target systems
buildSteps.detail: Theory predicts the strongest signals from close-in giant planets orbiting stars with strong magnetic fields and dense stellar winds.

buildSteps.title: Build or schedule the array
buildSteps.detail: At least a few hundred dipoles spread over hundreds of metres to a kilometre, on a radio-quiet site, tuned for roughly 10–200 MHz.

buildSteps.title: Observe for hours
buildSteps.detail: Several hours of integration per system, repeated over multiple nights and epochs to beat down noise and to distinguish a persistent source from a transient.

buildSteps.title: Form simultaneous beams
buildSteps.detail: One beam tracks the star while reference beams track sky positions a few degrees away and an empty patch, all at the same frequency; this measures the local confusion limit.

buildSteps.title: Excise interference
buildSteps.detail: Flag channels contaminated by FM, digital audio, aircraft and lightning, then re-derive the bandpass and correct for the ionosphere.

buildSteps.title: Search for narrowband drifting features
buildSteps.detail: Emission is expected at a cyclotron frequency set by the planet's magnetic field, strongly circularly polarised and drifting slowly in frequency as the field sweeps past the observer.

buildSteps.title: Vet candidates
buildSteps.detail: Require the signal to track the star's sidereal position, to persist across epochs, to be absent in the reference beams, and to have a polarisation signature no known interference source produces.

buildSteps.title: Interpret magnetism
buildSteps.detail: Convert the detected frequency to a magnetic field strength at the emission site and compare with models of the star–planet interaction and of atmospheric escape.

prerequisites.why: LOFAR, NenuFAR, the upgraded GMRT and the Murchison Widefield Array already cover 10–300 MHz; SKA-Low extends this with far greater sensitivity.
the same mechanism is measured from Jupiter's interaction with its moon Io, giving the template for what to look for.
at these frequencies interference can outshine the target by orders of magnitude, so sensitivity is limited by flagging quality as much as by dish area.
signals are weak and may drift, so hours of phase-coherent averaging and precise ionospheric calibration are needed.
predictions of how much power a star–planet interaction radiates span several orders of magnitude, which sets how long a search must be.

pathway.milestone: surveys of nearby systems with existing metre-wave arrays, yielding mostly non-detections plus a handful of contested candidates including a red-dwarf system
pathway.unlocks: first observational limits on exoplanet magnetic fields and a growing catalogue of the best targets.

pathway.milestone: SKA-Low and upgraded low-frequency arrays reaching microjansky sensitivity over wide fields
pathway.unlocks: faint enough to test the full range of predicted emission strengths for hundreds of nearby stars, not just the most optimistic few.

pathway.milestone: confirmed detections cross-matched with other magnetospheric tracers such as ultraviolet aurorae and star–planet interaction in stellar chromospheric lines
pathway.unlocks: a calibrated method for measuring exoplanet magnetic fields from the ground.

pathway.milestone: routine magnetic-field measurements for planets in habitable zones, feeding atmospheric-escape and habitability models
pathway.unlocks: knowledge of which planets keep their atmospheres and water over billions of years.
